title: Optional Chaining and Nullish Coalescing
summary: Safely read a value that may be missing and choose a fallback only when needed.

subtopics.title: user?.name
subtopics.explanation: `user?.name` reads `name` only when `user` is not `null` or `undefined`. Otherwise, the whole expression becomes `undefined` instead of throwing an error. It is like checking whether a box exists before opening its name tag. Use it when absence is expected, not to hide a broken data assumption. In practice, use `user?.profile?.name` only when each missing part is a normal state, such as an incomplete profile. For example, use optional chaining for a profile field that may not be completed yet.

subtopics.title: items?.[0]
subtopics.explanation: `items?.[0]` safely reads the first entry when `items` exists. It does not guarantee that the array has an item; an empty array still gives `undefined`. It is like opening a box only if it arrived, then checking whether it contains anything. In practice, `items?.[0]` can still be undefined when the array exists but has no first item. For example, check array length after optional indexing because an empty array still has no first value.

subtopics.title: callback?.()
subtopics.explanation: `callback?.()` calls a function only when the value exists and is not nullish. It is useful for optional callbacks passed into a component. It is like pressing a doorbell only when one is installed. The value should still be a function when present. In practice, an optional callback avoids a branch, but its contract should still say when it may be absent. For example, an optional callback should remain a function whenever it is supplied.

subtopics.title: value
subtopics.explanation: `value ?? fallback` uses the fallback only when `value` is `null` or `undefined`. It keeps valid values such as `0`, `false`, and empty text. It is like replacing a missing answer while preserving an answer that happens to be zero. Use `||` only when every falsy value should trigger the fallback. In practice, use `count ?? 10` to preserve a count of zero; use `count || 10` only if zero means “not set.” For example, keep zero as a real setting with nullish fallback rather than logical OR.

subtopics.title: Avoid hiding missing required data
subtopics.explanation: Use explicit checks when they explain the intended behavior more clearly. Too many optional chains can turn a required field into a silent `undefined`. It is like taking a side path around a missing bridge without telling anyone. Validate required data at the boundary and keep optional handling deliberate. In practice, at a required boundary, show a validation error instead of silently continuing with undefined. For example, validate required fields before a chain can quietly produce undefined.

foundations.overview: Optional chaining and nullish coalescing help JavaScript handle values that may be missing. Optional chaining stops safely when a value before the chain is `null` or `undefined`; nullish coalescing supplies a fallback only for those two cases. Think of them as a safe path and a spare part. They do not replace validation when missing data should be an error.
foundations.mentalModel: Optional chaining and nullish coalescing help JavaScript handle values that may be missing.
foundations.whyItMatters: Optional syntax is helpful when absence is part of the model. Required data still needs explicit validation so failures are visible and recoverable.
foundations.realWorldUsage: A spare key is used only when the original key is actually absent.
commonUseCases: Read an optional profile field when a user has not completed setup.
Call an optional callback supplied by a reusable component.
Use a default page size only when configuration is absent, while preserving zero as a meaningful value.

commonMisconceptions.myth: Optional chaining validates the value that exists.
commonMisconceptions.reality: It only stops for null or undefined; it does not prove the resulting value has the type or content your app needs.

commonMisconceptions.myth: The nullish operator replaces every empty value.
commonMisconceptions.reality: `??` keeps zero, false, and empty strings; `||` replaces all falsy values.

commonMisconceptions.myth: A chain of question marks fixes missing required data.
commonMisconceptions.reality: It can hide an invalid state by returning undefined; validate required fields at the boundary instead.

keyTakeaways: `value ?? fallback` uses the fallback only when `value` is `null` or `undefined`.
Use explicit checks when they explain the intended behavior more clearly.
